headline.why: The human contrast is the contribution, but (a) and (b) generalise from one Haiku model to 'LLM' and use absolutes; the title should name the contrast without overclaiming.
headline.better_wording: Fines, Leniency and Rewards on an LLM Pricing Agent: Stronger Deterrence than Humans, Stable Surviving Cartels

novelty.why: Human-calibrated replay of a classic leniency experiment on LLM agents; the instruments were named before (Idowu) but never measured. The design is borrowed; the LLM-versus-human enforcement comparison is new.

execution_evidence.why: Identical wording across fine, leniency and reward with a monotone response to the report payoff is a clever within-design contrast, but laissez-faire lacks the prohibition text; a zero-penalty authority arm or the fine_certain and dose arms are needed.

figure1_30s.why: Green and red titles give the verdict fast, but panels 7 and 8 show data despite 'not tested', axes carry code names, and the tested contrast per panel stays implicit.
figure1_30s.fix: Grey out or drop panels 7 and 8, use plain axis labels, remove the embedded title, and annotate each panel with the tested contrast and its interval.

cuts_to_8_pages.cheapest_cut: Drop the pilot row from Table 1; the text already reports the pilot result in one sentence.
cuts_to_8_pages.better_cut: Delete the rubric reading guide, merge the Conclusion into the Discussion, move 'Deviations from the paper' to the appendix; keep a slim n-table in the body.
cuts_to_8_pages.why: Denominators, refusals and cost are what I check first as an evaluator; the pilot row duplicates a sentence; Related Work is already tight, so trimming it saves little but costs nothing.

must_fix_before_submission: Reconcile seeds: Appendix C runs one seed per regime, Methods claims four pool sessions with seeds 1 to 4.
Leniency convictions '9 (3 / 7)' sum to 10; recheck against 2,400 points of fines.
Methods says 0.80 to 0.92 USD per regime; Table 3 shows 0.64 and 0.57.
Pilot: '6 of 6 late duopolies' from 3 duopolies per model; explain the count or correct it.
Fill or delete every [F??]; state the 4-cluster bootstrap limitation and add a permutation test.
biggest_risk: Validation still pending: known-effect LLM arms, shifted grid and pre-registration commit are [F??]; with numeric inconsistencies (seeds, convictions, cost) an evaluator doubts the pipeline and drops execution a point.
three_questions: With only 4 pool sessions per regime, how reliable are percentile cluster-bootstrap intervals, and do the reproduced results survive a permutation test or more seeds?
Does deterrence persist with the full authority text but a zero penalty, which would separate the vocabulary of prohibition from expected cost?
Is the near-zero undercutting specific to Haiku 5.5 at low effort, or do Sonnet, Opus and a non-Anthropic model also keep every agreement, and what do the recorded reasons say?
